clue.text: Some lunch efficiently produced by him?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark on a well-organised midday meal and the person responsible for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook in a restaurant kitchen is the one who prepares the meals served.

clue.text: Feline impressionists, perhaps

parts.note: imitators who mimic others, playfully pictured as cats doing impressions

explanation.surface: Cats doing impressions of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: People who imitate others; literally, cats doing imitation.

clue.text: Sacked a member of parliament that's vaporously explosive

parts.note: fired means dismissed from a job

explanation.surface: A dismissed politician causes an explosive scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A methane-rich gas found in coal mines that can ignite in an explosion.

clue.text: Succeed as fisherman, not as rower

explanation.surface: Something that counts as success for an angler but failure for an oarsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, this phrase means fouling the stroke by getting the oar caught in the water, a classic blunder; for a fisherman, literally landing a crustacean is a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, an angler landing a crustacean has done well; figuratively, a rowing blunder in which the blade jams in the water.

clue.text: Name of European lake uses no accents by design

indicators.note: the letters are arranged deliberately into a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lake's name is written without any diacritical marks on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bodensee, bordering Germany, Austria and Switzerland, is known in English by this name, which is also a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The English name for the Bodensee in central Europe, and also a girl's name.

clue.text: Simple alternatives allowing no negotiation

parts.note: a final offer with just two options: accept it or reject it, no haggling

explanation.surface: A blunt final offer in a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed offer to accept wholly or refuse, with no bargaining.

clue.text: Such a competitor is out of place

definitions.text: Such a competitor is out of place

parts.words: Such a competitor is out of place
parts.note: in a race, a runner who finishes outside the placings, not first, second or third

explanation.surface: A remark that a contestant does not fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser in a race or contest, unplaced among the winners.

clue.text: It will bear driver's overheads

parts.note: a frame on top of a car carrying luggage above the motorist's head, not business costs

explanation.surface: Something that pays a motorist's running costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame fitted on top of a car to carry luggage.

clue.text: Dough, or what it makes

explanation.surface: Raw dough and the loaf it turns into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' is slang for money, as is the answer; dough also bakes into a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for money, like dough; and the baked food made from dough.

clue.text: Benefactor of two boys

parts.note: Pat is a boy's name, short for Patrick
Ron is a boy's name, short for Ronald

explanation.surface: Someone who supports a pair of young lads financially.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor or supporter who gives money to a cause is its backer.

clue.text: Vital support of part of piano sound

parts.note: the keys are the part of a piano that is played
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: Something essential underpinning a component of a piano's sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the pieces: the piano's keys followed by their tone.
explanation.definitionFit: The central wedge at the top of an arch holds the rest in place, hence anything crucial to a structure.

clue.text: Merit tick

explanation.surface: A teacher's mark of approval on homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' is British slang for buying now and paying later: 'on tick' means on account.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve recognition is to earn praise; deferred payment, slangily called tick, is another word for the same thing.

clue.text: Experimenting, find rare type of radiation

indicators.note: trying things out in different ways suggests these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scientist trying things out discovers an unusual form of radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: Electromagnetic waves just beyond the red end of the visible spectrum, felt as heat.

clue.text: It is unlike feminine conversations to be frank

definitions.text: It is unlike feminine conversations to be frank

parts.words: It is unlike feminine conversations to be frank
parts.note: a talk between two males, in contrast to chats between women, and also a candid, direct exchange

explanation.surface: A rather old-fashioned claim that women's chats are never candid.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an honest, direct discussion, literally one between two males.

clue.text: Reversing order from the military man in charge

definitions.text: Reversing order from the military man in charge

parts.words: Reversing order from the military man in charge
parts.note: a parade-ground command from an officer telling soldiers to face the opposite way

explanation.surface: An officer cancels his earlier instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill command to turn to face the opposite direction, and figuratively a complete change of policy.

clue.text: Drink keeps hot in vessel

indicators.note: the word for drink holds the next letter inside it, as a container keeps something

parts.note: to sip is to drink in small mouthfuls
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A hot beverage is kept warm aboard a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A seagoing craft, as 'vessel' means a boat.

clue.text: Advise a student to be relaxed

parts.note: to inform is to tell or advise
L is for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: Telling a pupil to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual and without ceremony.

clue.text: Slip dollar to child

parts.note: the dollar sign $ looks like an S
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: Secretly passing a dollar bill to a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide or loss of grip, as of tyres on ice.

clue.text: Hard looks?

parts.note: not stern glares but thorough, intensive hunts for something

explanation.definitionFit: Thorough hunts for something, as police make of a house.

clue.text: Champion who will have to yield in the final analysis

definitions.text: Champion who will have to yield in the final analysis

parts.words: Champion who will have to yield in the final analysis
parts.note: a titleholder protecting a crown, who must eventually lose it

explanation.surface: A title holder must eventually give way.
explanation.definitionFit: A reigning champion protecting a title against a challenger.

clue.text: Congratulations as water supply completed

parts.note: a well supplies water from underground
done means finished

explanation.surface: Praise for finishing a project to bring water to a village.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of praise for a job well achieved.

clue.text: Wind coming with bad weather

indicators.note: something bad is spoiled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gales arriving with a spell of foul weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist or coil around, as a vine does round a post.

clue.text: Slattern, one leading a republic

indicators.note: the first pieces come in front of the final A, leading it

parts.note: a sloven is an untidy, slovenly person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A slovenly woman ends up as head of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A central European state, formerly part of Yugoslavia, governed as a republic.

clue.text: Look briefly over page in stint

parts.note: to skim is to read quickly over

explanation.surface: Glancing at a page during a spell of work.
explanation.definitionFit: To stint is to be sparing or economise.

clue.text: Boy from 8 put in the high chair

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
the boy's name in the answer to 8 across is Ron

explanation.surface: A lad is lifted into a baby's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's elevated seat of state.

clue.text: Young to have a time in lock up

indicators.note: the article and abbreviation are placed within the word for lock up

parts.note: to immure is to imprison or wall in

explanation.surface: A juvenile is given a spell in custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Not yet grown up or fully developed.

clue.text: Defend revolting Henry who is getting on

parts.note: people in revolt are said to be up, as in up in arms
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
someone getting on in years is old

explanation.surface: Standing up for an elderly, rebellious man named Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or maintain, as a court backs a ruling.

clue.text: PM's Norma slept uneasily

indicators.note: restless, uneasy sleep suggests the letters are tossed about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's wife Norma had a restless night.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Palmerston was a 19th-century British Prime Minister; Norma Major was a real PM's wife, adding to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian holder of Britain's highest political office, Prime Minister twice.

clue.text: Rise in pain, we hear

indicators.note: says the word for pain is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: sore means painful, an aching spot

explanation.surface: A pain gets worse, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb high, as a bird flying upwards.
